original_question: Let f : A^N -> A^N be a morphism over an algebraic closure of Q, written as polynomial coordinate functions f = (f_1, ..., f_N). If there is no non-constant rational function g with g o f = g, then there exists a point whose forward orbit under f is Zariski dense.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 13.2, titled "Orbit Density Conjecture for A^N," in §13; the immediately relevant nearby context is Definition 7.5 / Conjecture 7.6 on the fibering obstruction and Conjecture 13.5, the quasi-projective generalization. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper on the essential mathematical content: the ambient space is affine N-space over \bar{\mathbb{Q}}, f is written by polynomial coordinate functions, the obstruction is the existence of a nonconstant rational invariant g with g\circ f=g, and the desired conclusion is the existence of a Zariski-dense forward orbit. This is essentially the content of Conjecture 13.2. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
missing_details: It should be posed as a conjectural research question for general N, not as an established theorem: in this paper the statement is Conjecture 13.2, and the only case singled out as proved here is N=2 via Theorem 13.3. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

The rational function g should be identified explicitly as an element of the function field \bar{\mathbb{Q}}(x_1,\dots,x_N), i.e. a rational function on \mathbb{A}^N. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

The sought point should be stated explicitly as P\in\mathbb{A}^N(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}), and the conclusion should say its forward orbit O_f(P)=\{f^n(P):n\ge 0\} is Zariski dense in \mathbb{A}^N. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

The paper motivates the hypothesis by the fibering obstruction: a nearby definition says f is fibered if there is a positive-dimensional variety Z and a dominant rational map \psi:X\to Z with \psi\circ f=\psi. Including this context makes clear why invariant rational functions are the relevant obstruction. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

The nearby general formulation, Conjecture 13.5, is stated for a dominant morphism on a quasi-projective variety. If one wants the affine-space question to expose all hidden assumptions emphasized nearby in the paper, dominance should at least be flagged as part of the broader intended setting. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))

No degree, homogeneity, polarization, or other extra algebraic restrictions belong in this question; the paper states none in Conjecture 13.2. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
refined_question: For general N\ge 1, is the following Orbit Density Conjecture for affine N-space true: if f:\mathbb{A}^N_{\bar{\mathbb{Q}}}\to\mathbb{A}^N_{\bar{\mathbb{Q}}} is a polynomial self-map, written f=(f_1,\dots,f_N) with f_i\in\bar{\mathbb{Q}}[x_1,\dots,x_N], and there is no nonconstant rational function g\in\bar{\mathbb{Q}}(x_1,\dots,x_N) such that g\circ f=g, must there exist a point P\in\mathbb{A}^N(\bar{\mathbb{Q}}) whose forward orbit O_f(P)=\{f^n(P):n\ge 0\} is Zariski dense in \mathbb{A}^N? ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the affine-space statement in §13 rather than the broader quasi-projective statement in §13.1, because it keeps the ambient variety as \mathbb{A}^N over \bar{\mathbb{Q}} and writes f by coordinate polynomials. I therefore matched it to Conjecture 13.2 as the nearest official formulation, while using Definition 7.5 / Conjecture 7.6 to recover the intended obstruction-by-fibration context and Conjecture 13.5 to surface the nearby dominance language. Theorem 13.3 shows why the refined version should be phrased as an open question in general N: the paper records a proof only for N=2. ([rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu](https://rlbenedetto.people.amherst.edu/papers/ADtrends.pdf))
